chapter_title: Chương 63: 0063【Thất Bộ Thành Thơ? Biểu Diễn Trước Mọi Người】

segments.title: Chương 63: 0063【Thất Bộ Thành Thơ? Biểu Diễn Trước Mọi Người】
segments.content:
Zhang Xinping smiled faintly. "Don't be nervous. Just treat it like a normal chat."

"Alright," Chen Guiliang said.

Zhang Xinping: "What prompted you to participate in the New Concept Composition Contest?"

Chen Guiliang: "The college entrance exam score reduction."

Zhang Xinping: "Not a love for literature? Or perhaps the influence of your alumni?"

Chen Guiliang: "I'm a senior in high school."

Zhang Xinping: "What kind of books do you usually read? Be more specific. Don't just answer with two or three words."

Chen Guiliang: "I read everything. In elementary school, I'd pick up books from the trash heap. In middle school, I'd borrow wuxia novels from classmates. In high school, I'd look for books at used book stalls or pirated bookstores."

Zhang Xinping: "Picking up books from the trash heap?"

Chen Guiliang: "That's right. The village next to ours has a huge garbage dump, specifically for factory coal slag and city waste. The pencils I used in elementary school were all picked from that dump. I also found books like 'A Hundred Thousand Whys.' Even though they were stained and missing pages, they were enough to pass the time."

Zhang Xinping: "You're a kid from the countryside? Is your family very poor?"

Chen Guiliang: "I'm a 'left-behind child.' My family's situation is alright; we have enough to eat and wear."

The interview continued.

Zhang Xinping's questions were rather kind; she didn't try to make things difficult for a high school student.

Especially after hearing that Chen Guiliang was a left-behind child, she even deliberately kept her questions simple, wanting to shape the image of a rustic country boy who studied hard and loved literature.

The literary seminar had a basic procedure.

Li Qigang, the general director of New Concept, first gave a welcome speech, introduced the seminar's theme, and then introduced the participants present.

Then, Chen Guiliang, as the author, gave a rough overview of his essay.

"The preface, I won't go over. All the teachers here are clear on it."

"As for the poetry section, I'll explain the structure. This poem doesn't pile on ornate words; every line has a specific meaning."

"The first eight lines outline the entire story: a mystic bird breaks through chaos and flies to Yingzhou in search of immortals."

"The next sixteen lines elaborate on the process of seeking the immortals. This includes the help and encouragement the mystic bird receives, as well as the various dangers and difficulties it encounters, ultimately persevering and turning peril into safety."

"The following eight lines speak of how the rise and fall of ages are like clouds and smoke, yet the spirit of the mystic bird is eternal, and the children of Huaxia should inherit this spirit."

"The final four lines express my personal aspirations."

After Chen Guiliang finished speaking, a round of applause erupted.

It was the other first-prize winners who were clapping. They had already received the poem, but there were some parts they hadn't quite understood.

Moreover, some winners genuinely believed that Chen Guiliang had been piling on ornate words.

Now that he had explained it, it became much easier to understand when read alongside the poem.

The next segment was Q&A and discussion.

Wang Meng asked, "The Gushe Immortal and the Luochuan Goddess, what do you use them to represent?"

Chen Guiliang said, "They can be understood as the sages of past dynasties, the spirit they passed down encouraging the mystic bird to advance bravely. They can also be understood as the common people, good teachers and friends, who nurture, teach, and help the protagonist."

"What about the Kun Peng and the Horned Dragon?" Cheng Cun asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Forerunners. They were trapped, they all failed, but they left behind their tracks, providing the mystic bird with lessons and inspiration."

"Are you planning to study abroad?" Fang Fang asked.

"Huh?" Chen Guiliang looked completely baffled.

Fang Fang said, "Fangzhang, Penglai, and Yingzhou are the three immortal mountains overseas. Why is it that Penglai trapped the Kun Peng, Fangzhang trapped the Horned Dragon, but the mystic bird must go to Yingzhou to seek immortals?"

Chen Guiliang was a little annoyed. "This kind of most basic literary device, Teacher Fang Fang should be clearer on it than I am, right?"

Someone in the room chuckled.

Fang Fang's face turned cold, and she said no more.

In the end, Chen Guiliang still couldn't resist talking back.

After answering a few more questions, Wang Meng directly skipped the group discussion segment and proceeded to recite and analyze the poem in front of everyone.

Wang Meng said, "In the winter of the Guiwei year, I arrived in Shanghai, obtained a fable and wrote of its principle. These mere sixteen characters clearly explain the time, place, characters, and event. Especially the character '著' (zhuó, to write), it's used exquisitely. Changing it to '述' (shù, to narrate) wouldn't work; it would lose half its meaning..."

Once the poetry analysis was complete, the media reporters began to ask questions.

After all, they had been paid a handsome travel stipend.

The amount of the stipend determined which section it would be published in. Even within the same section, there were different positions.

Sprout had paid generously, so the reporters were naturally more proactive.

Dong Hongkang from the Wenhui Daily still believed that a high school student couldn't have written such an essay.

He planned to test his mettle on the spot: "Do you think you won first prize because you were lucky, or because you have real talent?"

As soon as he said this, the expressions of the people from Sprout and New Concept turned extremely ugly.

What did he mean by that?

Was he suspecting they leaked the topic, or suspecting someone had ghostwritten it?

Chen Guiliang faced him with a smile. "My luck is pretty good, and I have a tiny bit of skill."

Dong Hongkang said, "Your essay is absolutely stunning. I'll give you a topic now. How about you compose a classical poem on the spot? With your level, it shouldn't be difficult, right?"

"I'll give it a try," Chen Guiliang said.

Dong Hongkang had already thought of a topic: "Wild goose, small boat, river water, time. Use these four images to write a classical poem."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Do you want me to take seven steps?"

"Hahahaha!"

The room erupted in a wave of laughter.

He was using the story of Cao Zhi, complaining that Dong Hongkang was bullying him too much.

This topic wasn't actually difficult; it was nothing more than lamenting the passage of time and the fading of youth.

But how could you ask a teenager to write about that?

Even if he wrote it, it would be "composing new verses to force a feeling of sorrow." This kind of poem was more suited for the middle-aged and elderly.

Chen Guiliang could only stall for time. He said to Hu Weishi, "Sister Weishi, could you get me a brush, ink, paper, and inkstone?"

"I'll go look for them right away."

Hu Weishi quickly ran downstairs and called the magazine office. "Bring the brush, ink, paper, and inkstone. No need to be too fast."

They couldn't just wait around at the venue.

Another reporter asked, "Guo Xiaosi is your alumnus. What do you think about him being embroiled in a plagiarism scandal?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I haven't read either of those two novels, so I can't comment. But plagiarism is wrong."

Someone had already come up with a headline: Two Generations of New Concept First-Prize Winners Are Alumni; Junior Alumnus Scolds Guo Xiaosi for Plagiarism.

Among the reporters, Feng Wenya whispered, "Brother Dong, aren't you making things difficult for him?"

Dong Hongkang said, "Sprout insisted on inviting me. How can the literary supplement of the prestigious Wenhui Daily report irresponsibly? If I don't get this clear now, and some scandal about leaked topics or ghostwriting breaks out later, how will I explain it to my superiors then?"

"But the topic you gave is too difficult. He's only a teenager, how can he write it?" Feng Wenya said.

Dong Hongkang said, "Since Sprout invited me to promote him, he has to withstand the test! Judging by the level of classical Chinese shown in 'Voyage to the Sea of Ying,' this little poem shouldn't be hard."

The reporters continued to ask questions, not just of Chen Guiliang, but also of the other writers.

Yu Hua and Su Tong were whispering to each other, "Could you write it?"

Su Tong said, "I'd have to go home and think about it slowly. I couldn't write it on the spot. Chen Guiliang is quick-witted, and he knows how to stall for time."

Tie Ning was bent over, scribbling and doodling, trying to write that poem.

One by one, the reporters finished their questions, but the staff member delivering the brush, ink, paper, and inkstone still hadn't arrived.

The various media outlets grew more and more excited, purely enjoying the show and not minding if the situation got bigger.

If it was a small matter, they could make it bigger!

Hu Weishi stood at the entrance of the hall, waving frantically at Chen Guiliang, then pointing behind her, probably indicating that the things had arrived.

Chen Guiliang nodded slightly.

Hu Weishi wiped the sweat from her brow and had her colleague bring in the brush, ink, paper, and inkstone.

Chen Guiliang joked, "I think I'll take seven steps after all."

The paper and brush were placed in front of him. Chen Guiliang took seven steps in a circle, then picked up the brush, dipped it in ink, and flicked off the excess.

His calligraphy was average, but no one was paying attention to it now.

Many people crowded around him directly.

Dong Hongkang also stood beside Chen Guiliang.

It was one thing for him to test him with a difficult topic, but if Chen Guiliang could actually write it, and write it well, he was willing to promote this young man with all his might.

"A boat sails on the vast, misty waters."

There were too many people, and those on the outside couldn't squeeze in. A reporter helped read the first line aloud.

Line after line was read out, until the entire poem was finished. The hall suddenly fell silent for half a second.

Then it became lively again.

"A great poem!"

"Composing a poem in seven steps, I finally saw it with my own eyes today!"

"What seven steps? He stalled for half an hour."

"If you're so good, you write one."

"This time we have a topic for our report. It's definitely going to be eye-catching."

"..."

Chen Guiliang blew the ink dry, held the poem up to Dong Hongkang, and deliberately said in a literary tone, "A humble work, a gift for you, sir."

Dong Hongkang wasn't embarrassed at all. He accepted it with a wide smile and promised, "The day after tomorrow. Bi Hui will publish the full text of 'Voyage to the Sea of Ying' and this poem, and I'll write a review for you as well!"

He wasn't a reporter; he was a senior editor.

Bi Hui was the literary supplement of the Wenhui Daily. A few years ago, it held a writing competition with Ba Jin as the chairman of the judging committee. It also held essay contests, and people like Ji Xianlin submitted their work.

This supplement carried immense weight. For him to even show up today was a sign of respect, and now he was even promising to publish the article.

Dong Hongkang held up the paper, and on it was written—

A boat sails on the vast, misty waters, a goose flies past the edge of evening clouds.

This body is but a traveler against the current, why must one ask about the fleeting years?

The first two lines describe a scene, creating a very strong visual.

The last two lines offer a reflection, and an unconventional one at that. Instead of lamenting the passage of time, they are filled with the sharp spirit of youth, a kind of vigorous, soaring spirit.

It also perfectly incorporates the four keywords: wild goose, small boat, river water, time.

Fleeting years (liúnián) refers to the time that has passed.

For a reincarnator, the last two lines had another meaning, and Chen Guiliang had written them from the heart.

But if there were experts, they could still spot "flaws" in the writing.

Yu Hua muttered, "Fucking awesome!"

Wang Meng smiled without saying anything. He liked to support young people and was happy to see them shine.

Zhang Xinping, the reporter from the Shanghai Youth Daily who had interviewed Chen Guiliang earlier, was now quickly copying down this poem. She planned to go to Chen Guiliang's hometown for a more in-depth report!

For free, no travel stipend.

The other prize-winners, who had been watching the spectacle from afar, were now all dumbfounded with shock.

After the seminar ended, Li Haiyang went straight to a nearby internet cafe.

He logged into the Sprout forum, typed out the full text of "Voyage to the Sea of Ying" that he had copied, and posted it. Then he typed out the second poem and added an embellished account of what had happened.

What title should he give the post?

Li Haiyang thought carefully, then typed a line of text: Composed a poem in seven steps on the spot at New Concept. Are you impressed or not
